title: Deprecation telemetry and client-adaptive SDK strategy for contract evolution
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary: We need a pragmatic, observable approach to retiring legacy API behaviors and introducing new defaults for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. This ticket defines a two-part strategy: (1) server-side deprecation telemetry and enforcement thresholds to detect real customer impact early, and (2) a lightweight client-side adaptive SDK that negotiates behavior flags at runtime and provides safe fallbacks, auto-migration helpers, and opt-in toggles.

Background: Past deprecations caused higher-than-expected client breakage because we relied mainly on server-side logs and post-mortem bug reports. With richer realtime telemetry and an SDK that can adapt behavior per-route or per-deployment, we can reduce breakage while allowing us to move the platform forward (kernel changes, streaming shape changes, structured output tightening).

Goals:
- Instrument per-customer and per-route compatibility signals (rate of parsing failures, tool-call mismatches, trimmed streams, structured schema violations) and surface them in a deprecation dashboard.
- Define measurable thresholds that trigger pause / extended grace periods or rollout rollbacks.
- Build an adaptive SDK shim that: negotiates server-supported behavior flags at connection/setup time, exposes safe fallback APIs for tool calls and streaming, logs client-side compatibility events back to Redwood for correlation, and provides a one-line opt-in auto-migration utility for common schema changes.
- Create e2e backward-compat tests exercising streaming+toolcall interop across v{N} and v{N+1} contracts.

Non-goals: full blue/green multi-version serving (separate ticket), or forcing clients to upgrade; the SDK is intended to smooth upgrades not to force breaking changes.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Server telemetry granularity: per-token vs per-response. Per-response is cheaper and sufficient for structured output failures; per-token may be useful for strange streaming truncation patterns but will increase storage cost. We'll start with per-response plus sampled per-token traces.
- SDK complexity vs adoption: a heavy SDK that rewrites customer code will have low uptake. We will keep adapters minimal (behavior negotiation + small helpers) and provide idiomatic integrations for JS/Python/Go.
- Backoff and safety: SDK will enforce exponential backoff and fallback to a compatible contract when a client-specific failure rate crosses a threshold. That reduces immediate customer-visible errors but masks some server regressions; we will flag those in the dashboard for engineering attention.

Success criteria:
- Detection: actionable telemetry for 95% of active customers in rollout cohort within 48 hours of a contract change.
- Safety: reduce post-deprecation incident count by 60% compared to prior similar changes.
- Adoption: >= 40% of tracked SDK-using customers opt into adaptive SDK within first quarter after release; provide migration guide and examples.

Deliverables:
- Telemetry schema and collection plan (events, tags, retention).
- Deprecation dashboard prototype (internal).
- Adaptive SDK spec + JS prototype shim.
- e2e compatibility test suite and canary harness.
- Migration guide + Confluence doc + example PRs for customers.

Why this differs from prior efforts: Instead of only behavior flags and server-side graceful fallbacks, this work ties client-side negotiation and telemetry tightly into the rollout loop so product/eng can make real-time decisions based on per-customer signals and SDK-assisted fallbacks.

References and artifacts: see links below for initial design doc, prototype PR, and dashboard mockups.
updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created after post-mortem for streaming-toolcall schema tightening incident (PM requested proactive measures).

2026-03-06: Spike complete — JS SDK prototype that negotiates a 'compat' header and toggles a streaming fallback demonstrated; early results show fallbacks reduce user-facing errors by ~45% in a small internal cohort.
2026-03-08: Telemetry schema draft reviewed with Observability team; agreed on per-response event shape + sampled per-token traces. Added retention and PII filtering notes.

2026-03-09: Design review with PM (Aisha Rahman) and DevRel (Marco Delgado). DevRel requested migration snippets and a 'one-click' CDN import version of SDK. PM requested deprecation window policy baked into dashboard (see decision below).

2026-03-10: Scoping meeting with Runtime team — runtime will add a behavior_flags endpoint to expose server-supported flags per-model/version. Runtime agreed to a soft quota on sampled traces to limit cost.
comments: Aisha Rahman (PM) 2026-03-06: We need a clear SLA on telemetry latency — alerts should surface within 2 hours for high-impact customers.
Marco Delgado (DevRel) 2026-03-08: Keep the SDK ergonomics minimal: prefer a single 'negotiateBehavior()' API and a set of small utility functions rather than forcing a full client rewrite.
Sofia Martinez (Security) 2026-03-09: Ensure all telemetry is scrubbed for customer PII and that the SDK exposes no secrets. We'll require an internal security sign-off before public SDK release.
Design (Leah Kim) 2026-03-10: Dashboard mock looks good; add an at-a-glance 'compat health' score per-customer and allow filtering by route and model.
decisions: Use per-response telemetry as primary signal with 1% sampled per-token traces for deep debugging.
SDK will default to 'opt-out' on first release (customers must opt in), with incentives and clear migration docs; review after 3 months for opt-in->opt-out flip based on adoption.
Deprecation windows will be configurable but recommended defaults: 90 days for non-breaking contract softening, 180 days for changes affecting structured output schemas with high customer usage.
risks: Increased operational cost from sampled traces and retention — needs budget signoff.
Slow SDK adoption could leave many customers unprotected; fallback to server-side flags alone is less effective.
Complexity in edge-case negotiations between SDK fallback and runtime model routing could mask regressions if not surfaced properly.
next_steps: Deliver telemetry schema and open a telemetry collection RFC (owner: Evan).
Ship JS SDK alpha (negotiation + fallback) behind feature flag and onboard 5 internal customers (owner: DevRel).
Create e2e compatibility tests for streaming-toolcall interactions across v1/v2 contracts (owner: QA).
Implement deprecation dashboard prototype and wire basic alerts to PagerDuty for high-impact customers (owner: Observability).
Schedule security review and Confluence migration guide draft (owner: Security/Product).
